blocks.value: **Static variables and methods belong to a class as a whole, not to an individual object.**

items: **A static variable is shared by all the objects of its class.**
A static variable can be `public` or `private`.
Static variables that are not constants should normally be **private**, and accessed or changed only by accessor and mutator methods.
**A static method can be invoked without using any object.** It is invoked using the class name instead of an object name.
A static method is written with the `static` keyword in its heading.

blocks.value: `UnitConverter` is the class name; `convertFeetToInches()` is the static method.
**A static method cannot reference an instance variable of the class. It cannot invoke a non-static method of the class, unless it has an object of the class and uses that object in the invocation.**
That restriction has a simple reason: a static method may run when **no object exists**, so there is no instance variable for it to refer to.

`name` is per-object: each student has their own. `studentCount` is per-class: there is exactly one, and all three constructors incremented the same one. `getStudentCount()` is called on `Student` itself, before any object exists.

This also finally explains `public static void main`. `main` is static so the JVM can call it **without creating an object first**, and it is why calling an instance method directly from `main` produces `non-static method cannot be referenced from a static context`.
